memory_update.text: Politics themes often monetize through procurement, exemption paperwork, compliance, and supply-chain reconfiguration rather than direct end-demand alone.
Tier-2 and tier-3 defense suppliers are a priority underfollowed discovery lane because supply-chain visibility falls sharply below prime contractors.
A later layer should separate US defense, tariff, and election beneficiaries into distinct sub-themes to avoid overbroad theme dilution.

summary: Broad politics-driven market themes usually monetise through budget allocation, procurement, compliance, and supply-chain reconfiguration rather than through a single obvious end-demand surge. For this funnel, the highest-quality decomposition is to separate: (1) defense and homeland-security spending; (2) tariff-driven import substitution and exemption/admin burden; (3) election-driven policy volatility; and (4) regulation/compliance and government-capex execution. The underfollowed opportunity set is most likely to sit in obscure subcontractors, qualification-dependent components, testing/inspection, niche materials, and distribution/service layers that become more valuable when policy changes force re-sourcing or paper-heavy compliance.

theme_map.public_market_search_strategy: Start with broad policy regime mapping, then trace where the policy change forces a physical or administrative bottleneck. Prioritise suppliers one or two steps removed from the headline beneficiaries, especially small/mid-cap names with low analyst coverage, narrow customer exposure, and evidence of qualification lock-in, backlog, or mandated domestic sourcing. Use leaders as anchors, but search for hidden second-order beneficiaries in components, testing, logistics, compliance software, specialty materials, and subcontracting.
supply_side_constraints: Multi-tier defense and industrial supply chains with poor visibility beyond tier 2
Qualification and certification requirements that slow vendor switching
Case-by-case tariff exemptions and administrative overhead that weigh more on small suppliers
Scarce niche inputs such as rare-earth feedstock, specialty metals, and defense-grade components
Government budget timing and procurement lags that delay revenue recognition
